title: Dudo Error Envelope
description: The one error shape returned by every Dudo API, internal and public alike. This schema is a transcription of API_STANDARD.md §8 into a machine-readable form; it introduces no new decision and no new code. It is platform-wide rather than App-owned because an error shape that varies per module is not a shape. NOT EXECUTED: no JSON Schema implementation exists in this repository (AS1, TS1), so this document is normative and hand-checked, not machine-validated.

message.description: For a developer. NEVER contains business data, another tenant's identifiers, a stack trace, a query, a hostname, a library version, or internal structure (API_STANDARD.md §8, SECURITY_STANDARD.md §7). For a given code and a given failing condition the message is a fixed string that does not vary with the data involved — a message that varies with the record is a disclosure channel.

details.description: Machine-readable detail, under the same restriction as 'message'. Names the offending field and a stable issue token; never the offending value.

field.description: The request field, in wire form (snake_case), optionally dotted for nesting.

issue.description: A stable machine token, e.g. must_not_be_blank. Not a sentence, not the rejected value.

request_id.description: Returned on every response, success or error. It is what makes a support conversation possible without asking a customer to share their data (API_STANDARD.md §11). It is the ONLY identifier an error message carries — never a tenant id, never a resource id (MULTITENANCY_STANDARD.md §4 carrier 11).

retry_after_seconds.description: Seconds until the caller may retry. PRESENT ONLY ON 'rate_limited' AND 'quota_exceeded'. On every other code it is ABSENT — not null, not zero, absent — and that is enforced structurally by the 'allOf' below rather than left to be honoured. It is OPTIONAL even on those two codes: a value is not always knowable (a degraded coordinator does not have one), and a required field would be a field someone invents a number for. WHERE IT COMES FROM, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE OF WHY IT IS SAFE: it is derived from a FIXED WINDOW BOUNDARY — the end of the 60-second rate window, or the next 00:00 UTC reset — so it is THE SAME VALUE FOR EVERY CALLER ON THE PLATFORM AT THAT INSTANT, computable from a clock alone, and it carries no information about any Organization. It does not reveal which rate-limit level refused the request, because all levels share one window length. PROHIBITED, AND THIS IS THE CONSTRAINT AN OPTIMISER BREAKS: this value MUST NEVER be derived from observed usage, remaining budget, queue depth, current load, attempt count, or anything else a caller can vary. A retry time that reflects how much budget is left is a side channel on other tenants' activity — the same shape as the evaluation-position oracle closed one level up in customer-directory-v1.contract.yaml authorizationModel.budgetExhaustion, and reachable the same way, by a caller who deliberately drives the input it controls. A retry time that is a function of the calendar discloses nothing; a retry time that is a function of the system's state discloses the system's state. Only the first is permitted. This field also pays the debt API_STANDARD.md §10 records for 'rate_limited', which platform/core/http/api.ts names as owed and unpaid: the HTTP adapter emits the 'Retry-After' header DERIVED FROM THIS FIELD, so the envelope stays the single source of truth and internal, SDK and MCP callers — none of which see HTTP headers — receive the same value.

allOf.$comment: Presence rule for retry_after_seconds, expressed rather than described. Draft 2020-12 can decide this — 'if' with only 'else' is valid — and AUTHORIZATION_STANDARD.md §4 records what it cost the last time an expressible constraint was written up as prose. A retry time appearing beside 'not_found' would be a channel; here it cannot validate. NOT EXECUTED: no JSON Schema implementation exists in this repository (AS1, TS1), so like the rest of this document it is normative and hand-checked, not machine-validated.

errorCode.description: The closed taxonomy from API_STANDARD.md §8. An Action declares the subset it may return; anything outside that subset is a defect in the Action, not a new code.
